newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper buoyant, but RSI overbought.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper buoyant, but RSI overbought.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper's rally just above $2,500 late on Tuesday has left the market technically strong with the potential to extend gains further, traders and chartists said on Wednesday.
However, they noted that the 14-day RSI at around 76 percent was in overbought territory.
Downtrending charts might pressure aluminium lower.

COPPER - The market was set to test higher levels at $2,520 and $2,540 a tonne in the near term following covering from most quarters on Tuesday that moved prices to a one-year high just above $2,500.
"The threats of strikes in South America continue to be prevalent in the news, which is underpinning the copper market, as are the drawdowns in LME stocks," Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said.
Traders said a further fall in LME inventories on Wednesday might be enough to lift the market but they were also eyeing the 14-day RSI, which was overbought.

LME brokers Brandeis said a bullish outside day on the charts (on Tuesday) was countered by the seriously overbought condition. "We still view a correction as necessary before the market proceeds higher again," they said.
"This market is overbought so some consolidation may be seen with $2,462 offering good support," Harry Creates of AMT said.

On the fundamental front copper prices were seen remaining high over the next 12 to 18 months, with the market likely to be in deficit both this year and in 1998, according to Wiktor Bielski, senior commodities analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

Bielski told a conference in Seville on Tuesday, "The consensus view has been that the market has been about to move into surplus, but that view has been proved wrong over the last three years, when there have been deficits of between 100,000 and 250,000 tonnes."
At 0700 GMT three months copper was indicated at $2,500/$2,505, versus London's late close on Tuesday of $2,500/$2,504.
ALUMINIUM - Likely to be underpinned by any move higher by copper, though technically lacking upside momentum. "We are expecting further weakness," Squires of Wolff said.
Squires suggested the market could move to support at $1,634/37 and then $1,616.
But Gerald Metals said following on from Tuesday's bounce to a fairly positive close, aluminium was eyeing levels towards $1,700 if it could manage a constructive close on Wednesday.
Creates of AMT said that prices would find a block of resistance up to $1,678. He also pegged levels around $1,637 as important support followed by $1,627 and $1,622.
At 0700 GMT three months aluminium was indicated at $1,650/54, versus $1,648/51.
